highlights.description: Outlines: lay one agreement out in any organization's sections and order, with the same content digest
A crosswalk that shows where each section of another form is answered and what the agreement adds, as a command or an appendix
Hypotheses, milestone kinds, points of contact, a closeout, and signer capacity in the agreement

added.description: `pkg/engagement`: `Hypothesis`, `Milestone.Kind` (`kickoff`, `checkpoint`, `review`, `decision`, `final`, `closeout`), `Governance.Contacts`, `Closeout` with evaluations and reports, and `Signature.Capacity`, which is part of the content digest

The `outline` document kind: `engagement.Outline` with sections drawn from named blocks, optional `numbered` and `information` switches, and `datePrecision: month`; a generated, embedded `outline` JSON Schema; and `engagementio.LoadOutline` and `LoadDocument`
`pkg/outline`: the blocks an outline can name, party-role and milestone-kind filters, which blocks have content for an agreement, and the built-in outlines `full` and `summary`
`pkg/crosswalk`: for each section of a target outline, the sections of the rendered agreement that answer it, and the sections it does not ask for, with a Markdown table
`pkg/render`: `Options.Outline` and `Options.Crosswalk`; Hypotheses and Closeout sections, a milestone Kind column, points of contact, a short deliverables table, and month dates
Lint rules `unknown-reference`, `contact-party`, `hypothesis-untested`, `no-kickoff`, `no-closeout`, and `no-client-contact`; outline rules `unknown-block`, `duplicate-heading`, and `empty-section`
The CLI: `--outline` and `--crosswalk` on `render` and `export`, the `crosswalk` command, and `outline list` and `outline lint`; `validate` and `fmt` accept outlines

changed.description: The footer and information table name the layout when it is not the full agreement; with no outline, output is unchanged

tests.description: The fictional example gains hypotheses, contacts, and a closeout, with a fictional work plan outline and golden files for the one-page plan, the work plan layout, and the crosswalk appendix

documentation.description: The PRD, TRD, and roadmap specify alignment with other forms (Phase 5); the README describes outlines and the crosswalk

highlights.description: A Go-first model of a consulting agreement (a proposal or statement of work) with a generated, embedded JSON Schema
20 lint rules for what a schema cannot check: unique IDs, references, dates, commercials, lifecycle, and gaps such as nothing out of scope or no client responsibilities
Deterministic rendering to Markdown, and export to DOCX and PDF through Pandoc, with a printed signature block
A content digest printed on every document that ties a signed PDF to its exact source

added.description: `pkg/engagement`: the `Agreement` document with parties, people, background, objectives, scope with included and excluded items, phases, deliverables with acceptance criteria, milestones, responsibilities, governance, assumptions, risks, success criteria, acceptance, commercials, change control, terms, open questions, and signatures

Enumerations with `All…`, `Valid`, and `Label` helpers: kind (`proposal`, `statement_of_work`), status, party role, commercial model (`pro_bono`, `fixed_fee`, `time_and_materials`, `retainer`), and signature method
The `agreement` JSON Schema, generated from the Go types by `cmd/generate-schema` and embedded in `schema` with `Names`, `Get`, `Compiled`, and `Validate`

`pkg/engagementio`: YAML and JSON loading with size limits, schema validation, and strict decoding; canonical formatting; and `ContentDigest`, a SHA-256 of the agreed content that ignores status and signing records
`pkg/lint`: 20 rules in two severities, with findings in a fixed order
`pkg/render`: Markdown in Pandoc and GitHub flavors, with a document information table, numbered sections, a page footer in PDF output, and signature blocks
`pkg/pandoc`: the Pandoc command for DOCX and PDF, with timestamps pinned to the agreement's date, LuaLaTeX as the default PDF engine, and `NormalizeZip` for reproducible DOCX files

tests.description: A fictional pro bono example with golden Markdown in both flavors, a test for every lint rule, schema drift and determinism tests, and CLI tests

documentation.description: PRD, TRD, PLAN, and ROADMAP for the initiative, a README, and contributor guidance

infrastructure.description: CI, lint, and CodeQL workflows, and golangci-lint configuration
